nodes.description: Individualized balance, gait and strength training, mobility aids and fall-prevention adaptations support function. Goals and intensity depend on impairment and safety; rehabilitation is not established as a cure or proof of slowed molecular degeneration. A 62-person assessor-masked trial found greater SARA improvement with aerobic than dose-matched balance training; 43 participants had genetically confirmed SCA and the remainder had idiopathic ataxia or MSA-C. Selection required ambulatory function and safe cycling. This supports functional rehabilitation, not subtype-specific neuroprotection. In a separate uncontrolled seven-person SCA6/SCA31 cohort, annual intensive rehabilitation accompanied relative pre-session SARA stability through year six, while balance declined earlier; six-month follow-up SARA worsened from year three. Absence of a concurrent control prevents attributing long-term disease slowing to that regimen.
